observations.finding: At identical contrast settings fields contain far fewer cells than DMSO control (~40-60 cells/field vs dense confluent sheets of >150 in DMSO) and cells are isolated, compact, often triangular/rounded with reduced cell-cell contact.

data.note:
Specimen s_dc9b1c73e4 unblinded as anisomycin (PubChem CID 253602, identity check passed; CHEMBL423192, no curated mechanism in ChEMBL but BBBC021 annotates as Protein synthesis). Final conclusion Protein synthesis correct.

Reflection: Initial Actin disruptor call was driven by extreme act_mean z +28 to +58 and microscopist description of bright aggregated F-actin, but reviewer correctly flagged non-selectivity: act_tub_ratio ~0 with parallel tub_mean increase (z +5.9 to +12) and DNA/nuclear changes, consistent with broad translation-inhibition toxicity rather than selective actin action. Atlas NSC was 2/4 Protein synthesis vs 0/4 Actin (k-neighbours 5/10 Protein synthesis, 1/10 Actin), and the cleaner 0.3uM dose where act_mean already +28 still voted Protein synthesis (e20). Single-replicate design overstated confidence at 0.56.

Literature context: anisomycin is a classic ribosome-targeting protein synthesis inhibitor quantified in recent global nascent proteomics studies (PMID 37275259) and discussed for dissociation of JNK vs synthesis inhibition effects (PMID 24333448). Protein synthesis arrest secondarily remodels actin cytoskeleton/morphology in phenotypic screens (general mechanism reviewed in actin morphology literature, e.g., PMID 38290667 framework).

Lesson: weigh NSC prior and selectivity ratio over single-channel z-scores; require dose-dependent selectivity check before overriding atlas.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is anisomycin (PubChem CID 253602, e24/e25 name and BBBC021 structure agree, ChEMBL no curated mechanism) and scorer verdict is correct: final agent call Protein synthesis matched truth Protein synthesis. The trajectory is informative because it contains an initial incorrect call that was overturned on review, both at low confidence (p=0.56 Actin disruptors -> p=0.50 Protein synthesis).

What the evidence got right: The reference atlas consistently did not support Actin disruptors. At 2 wells NSC was already Protein synthesis 1/2 with k-neighbours Protein synthesis 5/10 vs Actin absent from top 3 (e4), and at 4 wells NSC was Protein synthesis 2/4 with nearest-neighbours Protein synthesis 5/10, Microtubule destabilizers 3/10, Epithelial 1/10 (e8). Re-evaluation of the cleaner mid-dose 0.3 uM well alone (e6: act_mean z=+28.4 already elevated but before massive toxicity) still voted Protein synthesis (e20), and per-well assessment of the 10 uM well (e3) showed Microtubule destabilizers 2/5, Protein synthesis 2/5, Actin disruptors 1/5 (e21) - 0/4 NSC votes for Actin overall as the review noted. Dose-responses for selectivity that I initially ignored were the key contra-evidence: act_tub_ratio rho=+1.00 p=0 (e18) with tub_mean rho=+0.80 (e19) rising in parallel to act_mean rho=+0.80 (e9) and act_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 (e11), plus nuc_dna_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 (e15) and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 (e13) brightening together. This non-selective multi-channel brightening with nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 (e10) and cell_count rho=-0.80 (e12) / microscopist "density lower vs DMSO" (e5) is consistent with protein-synthesis / runner-up toxicity rather than selective actin action, as the review stated (act_tub_ratio ~0).

What misled me and why: My acquisition choice and weighting were wrong. I sampled the most extreme high-dose wells first: 1 uM w_8e60c73d1a act_mean z=+58.3, act_glcm_contrast +48.6, act_std +31.0 (e2) and 10 uM w_55e65aedb1 act_mean +47.0, act_glcm_contrast +32.6, nuc_form_factor -39.7 (e3). Those extreme z-scores, plus the microscopist description on only 4 fields giving candidates "Actin disruptors" (e5), drove hypothesis step 16 to Actin disruptors 0.54 vs Protein synthesis 0.25 with e2/e3/e5/e6/e9/e10/e11 cited as support. I treated dose-dependent actin hyperintensity as selective, despite the atlas split (e4/e8) already contradicting it, and I submitted Actin disruptors p=0.56 with that rationale. I also underweighted that all calls were single-replicate across 4 doses (from e1: 8 doses available, we acquired only doses 3,4,5,7 once each e2/e3/e6/e7) and that rho=+0.80 trends were p=0.2 non-significant (e9/e11) while I over-interpreted them. The low-dose 0.1 uM w_c781542bcf with only modest act_glcm_contrast +5.4, cell_solidity +5.2, act_mean +5.1 (e7) should have alerted me that the huge high-dose signal was toxicity-associated.

What I missed until the review forced it: I did not compute selectivity until after submitting. Once e18 act_tub_ratio +1.00 and e19 tub_mean +0.80 showed parallel actin/tubulin/DNA rise, and e20/e21 showed even the cleaner 0.3 uM dose remained Protein synthesis by NSC, the actin hypothesis collapsed. Step 22 correctly re-weighted to Protein synthesis 0.50, Actin 0.25. The review's requested experiment - acquire dose 4 (0.3 uM) replicate 2 and compare to atlas/actin phenotype where act_mean already +28 but DNA effect low - could not be done due to spent budget, so overturn rested on existing e6/e20; a replicate would have tested whether Protein synthesis NSC repeats.

Literature in this run did not provide a curated ChEMBL MOA (e24/e25) but PubMed search "anisomycin protein synthesis inhibitor mechanism ribosome" (e26: 54 hits) and the title Anisomycin-induced protein synthesis inhibition PMID 24333448 are consistent with the unblinded truth; no specific paper in the returned list directly proves the actin-cytoskeleton confounding, so I make the selectivity-toxicity claim without citation beyond the screening metrics. Lesson: in cell-morphology screening, never call Actin disruptor on act_mean alone at high-dose extremes; require act_tub_ratio selectivity and independent atlas replication at a sub-toxic dose. This is a research screening reflection only, not clinical advice.

Selectivity metrics e18 act_tub_ratio rho=+1 and e19 tub_mean parallel rise plus e15 nuc_dna_mean +1 showed non-selective brightening, overturning selective actin

Missed that density loss (e5) + cell_count rho -0.80 (e12) + nuc_form_factor -39.7 (e3) and -1.00 rho (e10) signaled toxicity not selective cytoskeleton collapse

The trajectory is informative because it contains an initial incorrect call that was overturned on review, both at low confidence (p=0.56 Actin disruptors -> p=0.50 Protein synthesis).

What the evidence got right: The reference atlas consistently did not support Actin disruptors. At 2 wells NSC was already Protein synthesis 1/2 with k-neighbours Protein synthesis 5/10 vs Actin absent from top 3 (e4), and at 4 wells NSC was Protein synthesis 2/4 with nearest-neighbours Protein synthesis 5/10, Microtubule destabilizers 3/10, Epithelial 1/10 (e8). Re-evaluation of the cleaner mid-dose 0.3 uM well alone (e6: act_mean z=+28.4 already elevated but before massive toxicity) still voted Protein synthesis (e20), and per-well assessment of the 10 uM well (e3) showed Microtubule destabilizers 2/5, Protein synthesis 2/5, Actin disruptors 1/5 (e21) - 0/4 NSC votes for Actin overall as the review noted. Dose-responses for selectivity that I initially ignored were the key contra-evidence: act_tub_ratio rho=+1.00 p=0 (e18) with tub_mean rho=+0.80 (e19) rising in parallel to act_mean rho=+0.80 (e9) and act_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 (e11), plus nuc_dna_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 (e15) and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 (e13) brightening together. This non-selective multi-channel brightening with nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 (e10) and cell_count rho=-0.80 (e12) / microscopist "density lower vs DMSO" (e5) is consistent with protein-synthesis / runner-up toxicity rather than selective actin action, as the review stated (act_tub_ratio ~0).

What misled me and why: My acquisition choice and weighting were wrong. I sampled the most extreme high-dose wells first: 1 uM w_8e60c73d1a act_mean z=+58.3, act_glcm_contrast +48.6, act_std +31.0 (e2) and 10 uM w_55e65aedb1 act_mean +47.0, act_glcm_contrast +32.6, nuc_form_factor -39.7 (e3). Those extreme z-scores, plus the microscopist description on only 4 fields giving candidates "Actin disruptors" (e5), drove hypothesis step 16 to Actin disruptors 0.54 vs Protein synthesis 0.25 with e2/e3/e5/e6/e9/e10/e11 cited as support. I treated dose-dependent actin hyperintensity as selective, despite the atlas split (e4/e8) already contradicting it, and I submitted Actin disruptors p=0.56 with that rationale. I also underweighted that all calls were single-replicate across 4 doses (from e1: 8 doses available, we acquired only doses 3,4,5,7 once each e2/e3/e6/e7) and that rho=+0.80 trends were p=0.2 non-significant (e9/e11) while I over-interpreted them. The low-dose 0.1 uM w_c781542bcf with only modest act_glcm_contrast +5.4, cell_solidity +5.2, act_mean +5.1 (e7) should have alerted me that the huge high-dose signal was toxicity-associated.

What I missed until the review forced it: I did not compute selectivity until after submitting. Once e18 act_tub_ratio +1.00 and e19 tub_mean +0.80 showed parallel actin/tubulin/DNA rise, and e20/e21 showed even the cleaner 0.3 uM dose remained Protein synthesis by NSC, the actin hypothesis collapsed. Step 22 correctly re-weighted to Protein synthesis 0.50, Actin 0.25. The review's requested experiment - acquire dose 4 (0.3 uM) replicate 2 and compare to atlas/actin phenotype where act_mean already +28 but DNA effect low - could not be done due to spent budget, so overturn rested on existing e6/e20; a replicate would have tested whether Protein synthesis NSC repeats.

Literature in this run did not provide a curated ChEMBL MOA (e24/e25) but PubMed search "anisomycin protein synthesis inhibitor mechanism ribosome" (e26: 54 hits) and the title Anisomycin-induced protein synthesis inhibition PMID 24333448 are consistent with the unblinded truth; no specific paper in the returned list directly proves the actin-cytoskeleton confounding, so I make the selectivity-toxicity claim without citation beyond the screening metrics. Lesson: in cell-morphology screening, never call Actin disruptor on act_mean alone at high-dose extremes; require act_tub_ratio selectivity and independent atlas replication at a sub-toxic dose. This is a research screening reflection only, not clinical advice.

What was right:
- Atlas NSC and kNN consistently favored Protein synthesis over Actin (e4 1/2, e8 2/4, e20 0.3uM alone Protein synthesis, e21 high-dose only 1/5 Actin)
- Selectivity metrics e18 act_tub_ratio rho=+1 and e19 tub_mean parallel rise plus e15 nuc_dna_mean +1 showed non-selective brightening, overturning selective actin

What was wrong or missed:
- Initial p=0.56 Actin call overweighted extreme act_mean z=+58.3 (e2) and +47 (e3) and microscopist Actin candidates (e5) despite 0/4 Actin NSC
- Missed that density loss (e5) + cell_count rho -0.80 (e12) + nuc_form_factor -39.7 (e3) and -1.00 rho (e10) signaled toxicity not selective cytoskeleton collapse
- Understated discordance given single-replicate per dose design (e1-e7 only 4 wells)

Proposed next experiment: If budget allowed, acquire dose 4 0.3uM replicate 2 in MCF-7 Cell Painting with blinded atlas NSC/kNN and actin texture scoring; then orthogonal SUnSET puromycin incorporation / polysome profiling vs reference protein synthesis inhibitor to confirm translation block, plus G/F-actin fractionation to rule out primary actin MOA.
